newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Modise says no Syrian order for S.African arms yet.
newsitem.headline: Modise says no Syrian order for S.African arms yet.

text.p: South Africa's Defence Minister Joe Modise said on Wednesday Syria has not yet ordered tank sights from his country and his government would discuss the order when and if it is made.
Modise described as "lies" a report in a South African newspaper on Wednesday quoting him as saying the proposal to sell tank firing systems to Syria was off.

"There has never been an order from Syria. What happened is that one of our companies was marketing the tank sights and that is all. When there is an order and if there is an order, then we will discuss it," he told Reuters.
He was speaking on the sidelines of the IDEX international arms show in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates.
In Johannesburg, The Star newspaper reported Modise had announced South Africa wanted peace to prevail in the Middle East and had therefore decided not to continue with the proposed Syrian order.
Modise last month upheld South Africa's right to sell arms to Syria, accusing critics of the proposed $650 million sale of a laser-guided tank firing control system of pro-Israel bias.

Israel is worried by the proposed sale to its arch foe. The United States warned that selling the system to Syria would cost Pretoria $120 million of U.S. aid. President Nelson Mandela angrily called the U.S. criticism an afront to his country's independence.
